Whether as a result of new information, future events, changing circumstances, or any other reason after the date of this press release. Except as required by law.

I will now hand the call over to our President and Chief Executive Officer, Michael Scott Sarner. Thanks, Morgan. And thank you, everyone, for joining us for our second quarter fiscal year 27 earnings call. We are pleased to be with you today and look forward to discussing our results for the quarter. Our portfolio continued to deliver consistent results during the second fiscal quarter. We generated pre tax net investment income of $0.58 per share, which was supported by strong recurring earnings. Our undistributed taxable income balance remains robust. At $0.92 per share, reflecting consistent realization activity. We remain confident in our ability to continue covering both our regular and supplemental dividends throughout the earnings power of the portfolio.

Our board of directors has declared a $0.58 per share regular dividend for the December quarter paid out monthly over October, November, and December 2026. They have also declared a quarterly supplemental dividend of $0.06 per share payable in December, bringing total dividends declared for the third fiscal quarter to $0.64 per share. Deal flow in the lower middle market has been robust, The quarter was exceptionally active on the origination front, driven by both the strength of our sponsor relationships and the continued growth of our investment team. We closed a record $391 million in total new commitments across 14 new portfolio companies and 16 existing portfolio companies.

Our new portfolio companies this quarter span 11 industries, reflecting our ability to source deals across the lower middle market. For the new deals that closed during the September quarter, weighted average senior leverage was 3.4x debt to EBITDA and weighted average loan to value was 33%. Providing a substantial equity cushion beneath our debt. Our recent origination success has been supported by the sizable growth of our organization. Over the past 18 months, we have expanded our team from 27 to 46 employees, significantly increasing our sourcing and underwriting capacity. CapTrin, our strategic joint venture with Trinity Capital, has also broadened the range of opportunities we can competitively pursue.

Together, these efforts have helped us build a substantially larger pipeline. In fact, over the last 12 months, we have screened approximately 1.6 thousand opportunities, up from 1.2 thousand in fiscal year 26 and 1 thousand in fiscal year 25. And while our pipeline has grown, we remain highly selective with a close rate below 2 percent. We believe this reflects both our disciplined underwriting process and the depth of our relationships and sourcing capabilities in the lower middle market. Looking at the current macro lending environment, it seems more likely than not that we are heading back toward a higher for longer rate environment.

In a recent article, I discussed how a renewed rise in base rates could affect BDCs. The short answer is that higher rates are not simply good or bad for BDC earnings. Higher rates will certainly increase portfolio yields, but they can also put pressure on borrower cash flows and raise the BDC's own cost of capital. I think if rates move higher, you could see greater separation across the industry. With credit quality, portfolio company leverage, funding costs, and balance sheet liquidity becoming increasingly important differentiators. For Capital Southwest, we believe we are well positioned if rates move higher.

Our assets are predominantly floating rate, much of our debt is fixed rate, and our portfolio companies have conservative leverage of approximately 3.7x. We have also gained experience and insight from navigating the previous rate cycle. When SOFR rose above 5.5% and saw firsthand how our lower middle market portfolio performed. While every rate cycle is different, we believe the combination of our asset sensitivity, liability structure, and conservative portfolio leverage positions us well if base rates move higher. Beyond our core balance sheet activity, we continue to broaden the ways we attract investment opportunities. This quarter, we partnered with Trinity Capital to form Desert Star, our second joint venture together with a $25 million equity commitment.

Desert Star gives us access to technology lending market. Allowing us to gain exposure through a granular portfolio of investments in an area where we have not historically focused. We expect to deploy our equity commitment over several years as we take a measured approach to investing in this area of the market. Turning to our capital structure, we significantly strengthened our balance sheet during the quarter. We issued $350 million of 5-year unsecured notes and amended, extended, and upsized our corporate credit facility. This amendment meaningfully reduced our cost of capital while providing additional capacity and flexibility to support future growth. Following these transactions, we have no debt maturities until 2029.

In connection with the unsecured note issuance, we also entered into our first interest rate swap. Chris will provide more detail on these activities in his remarks. Rounding out a solid quarter, we raised $67 million in gross equity proceeds through our ATM program. Our ability to access this program continues to be a meaningful competitive advantage for Capital Southwest. In a market where fewer publicly traded BDCs are trading above book value, our improved price to book valuation gives us a differentiated ability to raise growth capital that is accretive to NAV and supportive of long term shareholder value. Boise Cascade (BCC) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

📅 Nov 03, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Hardie transition and affordability pressures shape the fourth-quarter outlook.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Boise Cascade Company (BCC +1.08%) reported increased revenue and net income for the third quarter despite a decline in total U.S. housing starts. Management focused on the operational transition to James Hardie as the exclusive supplier for siding and trim, while also integrating TimberTech and AZEK decking lines. The company reported that consumer affordability challenges and rising interest rates have constrained the new home market, leading to more conservative inventory practices among customers. Forward guidance for the fourth quarter reflects typical seasonal slowing and higher input costs, while the company maintains a disciplined approach to shareholder returns through dividends and share repurchases.

Pricing discipline cut sand volumes as its power build-out accelerated.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Atlas Energy Solutions Inc. (AESI -0.91%) reported third quarter results that demonstrated a strategic prioritization of pricing discipline in its proppant business and the acceleration of its power segment infrastructure. Management reported that the company deliberately reduced sales volumes to avoid uneconomic pricing, leading to a sequential decline in revenue and Adjusted EBITDA. The company stated that it has secured 1.4 gigawatts of power generation equipment through a frame agreement with Caterpillar and has entered into two cost reimbursement agreements with a frontier AI lab to backstop two large data center projects. To fund these initiatives, the company established a $424 million bridge facility, with plans to supplement debt with accretive equity only after definitive energy service agreements are executed. Management expects sequential improvements across all business segments in the fourth quarter, supported by a filled volume queue for 2027 and the anticipated commencement of operations at the Socorro power project in early 2027.

Whether that equity comes as common equity, subsidiary-level equity, or convertible debt, our objective is to choose the form and timing that minimizes dilution, and we'll judge it by one measure: cash flow accretion. Fourth, delivering the power. Socorro is a good look at how we execute. We signed the Socorro PPA on March 31. Today, all generator pads have been poured. The first gensets are on site. If there were an extended delay in Texas, our customer has opportunities in other states with clear permitting paths that require first power in 2027, and we would work with them to move the projects and the equipment there. These two projects will not be the end of our growth in this business.

We are seeing growing demand for behind-the-meter power for projects starting up in late 2028 and 2029, and we are having active conversations with our equipment providers to see what can be available and when. Blake McCarthy: Thanks, John. On our last conference call, I detailed how there continued to be some egregiously low-priced bids in the sand market from some of our competitors. During the quarter, our overall sales volume and Dune Express volumes were down due to the vacancies left by the rejected bids, leading to sand revenue being down 8.3% sequentially.

This resulted in higher OpEx per ton, particularly at our Kermit facility, with overall plant OpEx per ton of $13.96, including royalties. Overall OpEx per ton is expected to improve to approximately $13 per ton in Q4 and continue into 2027. Importantly, our commercial team has done a wonderful job of filling the volume hole left by the rejected customer volumes in Q3. Overall sales volume is expected to be up meaningfully from 5.4 million tons in the third quarter to 5.7 million-6.1 million in the fourth quarter.

As we mentioned on our prior quarter's call, RFP season for some of our key customers got started early this year. While sand pricing overall remains challenged, the accelerated RFP season has resulted in us having a line of sight on more than 23 million allocated tons for 2027, at pricing levels roughly in line with 2026 pricing already. We are well on our way to being fully utilized across our system for next year. Despite a strong commodity price environment, Permian operators have yet to really hit the gas pedal on activity, so our objective is to fill up the plants and begin moving price on the incremental ton.

While sand pricing remains stubbornly in the $16-$18 range, we are significantly more bullish on the outlook for logistics pricing. Throughout the year, we have seen steady increases in driver shortages and thus, in driver rates. As Atlas' logistical efficiencies provide us significant competitive advantages in the total delivered cost of sand, we used our advantaged logistics cost structure to sweat competitors who could not find drivers for a good part of the year. While this negatively impacted our logistics margin, it enabled us to capture incremental volumes for most of the year outside of the volumes we turned away.

However, the market has now reached a point where we feel it is not just possible, but necessary for us to push pricing. Through the oil field grapevine, we have heard of numerous instances of well sites dependent on competitor sand experiencing significant non-productive time. Cheap sand only saves you money if it shows up on time, and with a shortage of drivers in West Texas, driven by continued strength in the over-the-road market and the steadily growing sucking sound coming from the data center build-out market, the number of suppliers that can still ensure that the product gets to the job on time is shrinking rapidly.

We began passing through rate increases during the third quarter, which helped to lead to margins of approximately 11%, adjusting for expenses related to the closure of our Northeast region. With the anticipated improvement in Q4 delivered and Dune Express volumes, we expect logistics margins to improve to approximately 14%-15% during the fourth quarter and continued strength in 2027. Bud Brigham: Thank you, Blake. Every era of progress has been built on energy. The industrial age ran on coal and steam. Metallus (MTUS) Q3 2026 Earnings Call Transcript

📅 Nov 03, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

A $995 million defense contract and a CEO retirement shape this quarter.

Need a quote from a Motley Fool analyst? Email [email protected]

Metallus Inc. (MTUS -5.25%) reported its third consecutive quarter of year-over-year profitability growth and achieved its annualized sales target for the aerospace and defense segment. Management reported that the company reached a $250 million run rate in the aerospace & defense market and secured a new long-term contract with the Defense Logistics Agency. The company indicated that order book visibility extends into the second quarter of 2027, supported by a favorable pricing environment and steady demand in core markets. Additionally, the company is preparing for a leadership transition with the upcoming retirement of its chief executive officer at the end of the year.

Operator: Hello, everyone. Thank you for joining us, and welcome to the 3Q 2026 Metallus, Inc. Earnings Call. [Operator Instructions] I will now hand the conference over to Jenna Johnson. Please go ahead.

Jenna Johnson: Good morning, and welcome to Metallus' Third Quarter 2026 Conference Call. I'm Jenna Johnson, Senior Manager, Finance and Investor Relations for Metallus. Joining me today are Mike Williams, Chief Executive Officer; Kris Westbrooks, President and Chief Operating Officer; and John Zaranec, Executive Vice President and Chief Financial Officer. You should have received a copy of our press release, which was issued last night. During today's conference call, we may make forward-looking statements as defined by the SEC. Actual results may differ materially from those projected or implied due to a variety of factors, which we describe in greater detail in yesterday's release.

Please refer to our SEC filings, including our most recent Form 10-Q, which will be filed later today as well as the risk factors included in our earnings release, all of which are available on the Metallus website. Where non-GAAP financial information is referenced, additional details and reconciliations to its GAAP equivalent are included in the earnings release and the earnings presentation available on the Investor page at metallus.com. Now I'll turn the call over to Mike Williams for his remarks.

Michael Williams: Thank you, Jenna, and good morning, everyone. Our third quarter results reflect strong execution across the organization. Through a continued focus on operational excellence, commercial discipline and strategic initiatives, we increased profitability both sequentially and year-over-year for the third consecutive quarter. Additionally, we achieved our $250 million annualized aerospace & defense run rate sales target. This milestone was made possible by our dedicated teams working across the organization and expanding partnerships with customers in this market. During the quarter, we also reached several milestones that support our long-term growth strategy. In August, we commissioned the new strategic manufacturing assets supporting critical defense materials, a significant milestone in our long-term growth strategy. We were honored to host representatives from the U.S.

Army, regional economic development organizations, customers and government leaders as we showcased investments that strengthen the domestic munition supply chain and support U.S. national security. In late September, we were awarded a contract by the U.S. Defense Logistics Agency, or DLA, to supply steel for critical defense applications. The contract includes an initial delivery order valued at approximately $125 million and a ceiling of up to $995 million over a 5-year ordering period. The award reflects Metallus' ability to produce specialty steel products that meet the rigorous performance, quality and traceability requirements of critical defense applications. It also highlights our team's metallurgical expertise in partnering with our customers to find critical solutions for their evolving needs.

Additionally, we continue to gain traction with new participants in the defense market. We recently secured a $10 million purchase order from a new prime contractor for finished fully assembled components supporting a growing munitions program. This order is another sign that our capabilities and reputation are helping us provide solutions for new customers. Together, the customer momentum and recently achieved AS9100 certification provides external validation that our focus and investment in aerospace & defense is working. These wins are not isolated events. They reflect the sustained deliberate effort we have made to grow and deepen our presence in this expanding market. Finally, as previously announced, I plan to retire as Chief Executive Officer at the end of the year.

Kris Westbrooks, our President and Chief Operating Officer, will succeed me. This planned transition reflects the Board of Directors' commitment to a well-planned and seamless succession and positions Metallus to build on its established momentum into the future. With that, I'll turn the call over to Kris to walk through our third quarter highlights and end market performance in more detail.

Kristopher Westbrooks: Thanks, Mike. Good morning, everyone. I'll start with our third quarter highlights, then discuss demand across our end markets and close with our positive outlook for 2027. Third quarter adjusted EBITDA was $34.5 million, increasing 19%, both sequentially and year-over-year. The quarter benefited from a favorable product mix, record aerospace & defense sales and shipments and the continued impact of disciplined pricing actions. Turning to operations. Melt utilization reached 76% in the third quarter, excluding a 3 percentage point impact of electricity curtailments. Underlying operating performance improved during the third quarter despite the increased weather and grid-related disruptions. We continue to take steps to reduce the operational impact of electricity curtailments and meet growing customer demand.

Additionally, our team completed its planned annual shutdown maintenance at the melt shop in October. I'm encouraged by the melt shops performance to date in the fourth quarter following the shutdown maintenance. Turning to our end markets. As expected, automotive shipments and sales declined sequentially due to timing and were relatively flat year-over-year. Automotive is a core part of our portfolio and demand trends remain steady in this market, supported by a healthy order book. Our existing auto programs, platform wins and customer relationships provide a solid foundation. We remain focused on delivering the performance and partnership our customers expect. Industrial shipments declined slightly at 3% sequentially and year-over-year.

Spot price increases implemented throughout 2026 continue to benefit base sales per ton and total sales within the industrial market. Inventory levels in the industrial distribution supply channel remained low, reflecting strong demand and tight supply. A strong trade environment and ongoing supply chain reassessments are resulting in customers increasing their needs from domestic suppliers. This is supported by industrial bookings, which remain elevated compared with a year ago and positions Metallus to capture additional industrial opportunities. Leading our third quarter end market performance was aerospace & defense, or A&D for short. A&D shipments reached nearly 22,000 tons in the quarter, up 34% year-over-year and 10% sequentially. Net sales increased 41% year-over-year in the A&D market.

And as Mike mentioned, we achieved our $250 million annualized sales run rate target. Our continued progress in end market diversification is also improving profitability. While aerospace & defense accounted for 13% of total shipment volume, the A&D sales contribution was much larger at 20% of sales in the quarter. This underscores how higher-value A&D product offerings strengthen product mix and profitability. In Energy, shipments declined sequentially but increased year-over-year. The U.S. rig count is up approximately 10% from a year ago. We are seeing strong bar and tube demand signals from key customers. Energy remains a strategic market for Metallus.

And although energy shipments represent a smaller proportion of overall shipments, we see continued opportunities for growth in this sector. Finally, let me briefly update you on our 2027 outlook at a high level. Market conditions remain favorable, and our order book has grown both sequentially and year-over-year. These conditions provide solid visibility with customer orders booking into the second quarter at this time. The strong market demand, combined with our strategic advancements and continued operational execution, reinforces our confidence in another year of anticipated profitable growth as we plan for 2027. With that, I'll turn the call over to John Zaranec to walk through the financial highlights of the quarter.

John Zaranec: Thank you, Kris. During the third quarter, our team delivered improvements in profitability on both a sequential and year-over-year basis for the third consecutive quarter, consistent with our guidance. We also continued to diversify sales across our markets, expanding our margin through favorable mix. From a top line revenue perspective, third quarter net sales totaled $337 million, a year-over-year increase of $31.3 million or 10%, primarily driven by higher shipments in aerospace & defense and energy markets. Net income was $23.8 million in the third quarter or $0.55 per diluted share. On an adjusted basis, net income was $14.9 million or $0.35 per diluted share.

Adjusted EBITDA was $34.5 million in the third quarter, both a sequential and year-over-year increase of $5.5 million or 19%. The increased sequential profitability was primarily driven by improved base prices and mix, partially offset by planned shutdown maintenance timing, higher operating costs to support demand and an increase in electricity curtailments, as Kris previously discussed. In the third quarter, we generated $6.8 million of operating cash flow, reflecting solid profitability, partially offset by investments in inventory to support the continued ramp-up of our business and our annual insurance premium payment in July. In the third quarter, capital expenditures totaled $13.1 million, including approximately $4.9 million related to the projects primarily funded by the U.S. government.

Consistent with our previous communications, planned capital expenditures for the full year are expected to be approximately $70 million, inclusive of approximately $35 million of capital expenditures primarily funded by the U.S. government. At the end of the third quarter, the company's cash and cash equivalents balance was $98.6 million. As it relates to government projects, during the third quarter, as Mike noted, the company celebrated the commissioning of new assets supporting critical defense materials, and we further strengthened our long-term growth outlook with a new commercial DLA award, including an initial $125 million purchase order and a contract value of up to $995 million over the next five years.

We are currently establishing the production and shipment schedule for the initial DLA order as well as assessing any longer-term capital requirements. The first order must be fulfilled within two years of receipt, and we anticipate shipments to commence in the second quarter of 2027 and ramp further throughout the remainder of next year. Now switching to pensions. In the third quarter, the company made no required pension contributions related to the U.S. bargaining plan, consistent with our guidance. Based on our updated actuarial analysis, no additional pension contributions are expected for the remainder of 2026. As a reminder, our 2026 pension contributions represent a reduction of over 60% when compared to 2025.

In terms of shareholder return activities, in the third quarter, the company repurchased approximately 190,000 shares of common stock at a cost of $3.6 million. At the end of September, a balance of $78.2 million remained under our existing share repurchase program. Since the inception of common share repurchases in early 2022, combined with the convertible note repurchase activities, we've reduced diluted shares outstanding by a significant 26% or 14.2 million shares. These actions reflect the strength of the company's balance sheet and confidence in through-cycle cash flow generation. As it relates to liquidity, total liquidity remained strong at $389 million as of September 30, 2026. At the end of the third quarter, the company had no outstanding borrowings.

Turning to the near-term outlook. Commercially, fourth quarter shipments are expected to be lower than the third quarter by a high single-digit percentage, primarily due to normal year-end seasonality. However, shipments are expected to be higher when compared to the prior year fourth quarter. Lead times for bar and tube products currently extend into the second quarter of 2027. Based on lead times and anticipated product mix, fourth quarter price and mix are expected to be slightly lower than in the third quarter. The company recently announced price increases of $60 per ton on both bar and quench and temper seamless mechanical tubing, effective early October for customers not covered by annual pricing agreements.

Based on lead times and order backlog, the company expects to realize the benefit of these price increases ramping throughout 2027. We are also in the middle of our annual customer contract season. And while we expect pricing expansion when compared to last year's annual contracts, historically, the annual contract prices are lower than the spot price market increases. We will share more on the pricing impact on 2027 anticipated results during our year-end call in February.

From an operational perspective, annual shutdown maintenance in the fourth quarter is expected to unfavorably impact adjusted EBITDA by approximately $10 million to $15 million compared to the third quarter, reflecting incrementally higher shutdown costs, lower fixed cost leverage and lower melt utilization, consistent with prior year timing. And finally, an adjusted effective income tax rate between 27% and 30% is expected for the full year 2026. Given these elements, the company expects fourth quarter 2026 adjusted EBITDA to be lower sequentially but higher than the prior year fourth quarter. We expect full year adjusted EBITDA for 2026 to be between $100 million to $105 million.

Before we conclude today's prepared remarks, I would like to turn the call back over to Mike for some closing comments.

Michael Williams: Thank you, John. This is my final earnings call as CEO of Metallus. I'd like to take a moment to reflect on the company's progress over the past six years. Metallus is a stronger company today based on a strong foundation of metallurgical expertise and world-class specialty solutions. We have improved operational performance, strengthened our commercial discipline and invested in capabilities that differentiate us in specialty metals. But overall, we're encouraged by the work that's been done to date. And we do expect a net positive benefit from pricing to flow through the bottom line, and we'll provide additional information as we complete those negotiations and have our call in February.

David Storms: Understood. That's great color. I appreciate that. And then maybe just as a follow-up, I know I believe it was John's prepared remarks that you're still assessing new assets needed, capital requirements for the DLA project. With this initial order, maybe can you give us a sense of what your expectations were going into it? Do you think you have the capacity to fill this order and then maybe new assets would come with any follow-on orders? Or is there a different way we should be thinking about this?

Kristopher Westbrooks: We're currently working through that right now. We have capacity to start the order and deliver on our near-term commitments and ultimately fulfill it. It's just how do you balance that with our growth opportunities in other spaces within the defense area. So we're working through that right now. Even if we were to put in capital, you're a couple of years out from seeing the benefit of that. So our focus is on delivering that order with existing capacity and continuing to look for opportunities as it makes sense to grow the overall portfolio.

Operator: [Operator Instructions] Your next question from the line of Samuel McKinney with KeyBanc Capital Markets.

Samuel McKinney: Congrats to Mike on the retirement. It's been great working with you the last few years.

Samuel McKinney: In the industrial end market, it was made clear on the last earnings call that the backlog had nearly doubled year-over-year with strength in equipment and providing you strong visibility into second half shipments. With the third quarter shipments down versus the second quarter, I think it would be helpful if you could provide some more detail on that decline, whether it was prioritizing other end markets or simply demand that didn't come to fruition from some of those major industrial customers? Anything there would be helpful.

Kristopher Westbrooks: Thanks, Sam. Yes, that's a good point. Yes, we're still seeing solid demand from the industrial markets. The order book is up slightly, still at a solid level. We're seeing good demand from a construction equipment perspective as well as general machinery. What we did impact -- have impacted in Q3 was around the melt shop curtailments. That was a few percentage points of utilization, equivalent to about 10,000 tons of melt production, and that had to be distributed amongst our order book, and we felt some of the impact in the industrial markets in the third quarter impacting those shipments.

We still have good visibility into the future, and we're optimistic about where those markets, specifically industrial is going as we move forward, but you did see the lower shipments in Q3 as a result of that downtime.

Samuel McKinney: Okay. And then just given the strength of the overall steel market and continued price increases for you guys flowing into the order book, can you elaborate just a bit more on your expectation for fourth quarter pricing to decline sequentially? I assume it's a mix thing as you shift more focus to the base end markets like auto and industrial. But any more color would be helpful as we think through the end of the year.

Kristopher Westbrooks: That's exactly right, Sam. It's more of a mix element that we're experiencing in fourth quarter. There's no systemic changes in pricing. We're still seeing the benefits of what we implemented earlier this year as we head into 2027 as well. It's just the mix of products that our customers need in the fourth quarter that's going to drive, we believe, that base pricing to be down some.

Operator: Your next question from the line of John Franzreb with Sidoti & Company.

John Franzreb: Again, congratulations to Mike. Just on the DLA contract, I'm kind of curious about the timing of the flow-through of the revenue. How should we be thinking about that over the next year or two years? How does that timing kind of play out on the top line?

Kristopher Westbrooks: We expect it to ramp throughout 2027 into 2028. The order came in, in late Q3 2026. We have two years to supply that. Obviously, we want to fulfill that order efficiently as quickly as we can, but we also have other customer orders to balance. And our goal is to balance all of those while still supporting the DLA with their initial order. So we do expect it to ramp throughout the year, and it's going to hit the top line just like a regular sale into the aerospace & defense market.

John Franzreb: Okay. Kris. So it's not going to kind of -- you can use some downtime maybe and use that as an opportunity to maybe balance the shipments, nothing like that's going to happen.

Kristopher Westbrooks: With the current order book, I don't see that. And maybe in a weaker market, you would take a different approach. We're going to obviously make it as efficiently as we can. So if there's an opportunity to have a longer run of this product to drive efficiency and increase yield in our shop, then we're going to do that, and that will benefit everyone.

John Franzreb: Got it. And just maybe if you could provide a little bit more color what you're seeing in the automotive market. It was down sequentially, normally, third quarter is relatively strong in the auto sector. You just said that you expect it to be down a little bit in Q4. What are you anticipating in the coming quarters in the auto side?

Kristopher Westbrooks: It's been pretty steady. If you look at Q2 was a strong auto shipment quarter, which really drove some of the decline that you saw in Q3. And if you were to normalize for all of that, I think you look at our auto shipments as being up year-over-year, but fairly steady as we head into 2028. 2027, you'll see some programs beginning to drop off, and we're quoting new opportunities and it may even be in a different market like industrial, for example. So we're still well positioned there. It's an important part of our mix.

I think we finished in the high 30% on a percent of sales for the quarter in automotive, which is about what we're targeting.

Operator: There are no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back to Jenna for closing remarks.

Jenna Johnson: Thank you for joining us today, and that concludes our call.

Operator: This concludes today's call. Thank you for attending. You may now disconnect.

Tennessee ranks in top 10 of Nielsen index of best college basketball fanbases

📅 Nov 03, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

Tennessee has one of the top fanbases in the nation for men's and women's basketball, according to Nielsen's newest study.

The media audience research firm released its inaugural "Nielsen Scarborough Fandom Index" on Nov. 3, which ranks the country's most devoted fanbases by analyzing data across seven metrics – apparel purchases, event attendance, digital streaming, social media engagement, TV viewership, radio listening and overall interest level.

The inaugural index included the top 20 "most avid college basketball markets" for both men's and women's basketball.

Knoxville checked in at No. 8 with an index score of 178, which was the third-highest mark among SEC fanbases. Lexington (Kentucky) took the No. 1 spot, while Birmingham (Alabama) ranked No. 6.

Nielsen's research showed that smaller markets like Knoxville and Birmingham generate higher merchandise sales than big hubs like Atlanta, "proving that deep local affinity often generates higher marketing ROI than sheer audience size."

The Lady Vols have one of the biggest, most loyal fanbases in college basketball, built through legendary coach Pat Summitt's dynasty of eight national championships during her 38 seasons. The Vols have become one of the top programs in the SEC under Rick Barnes, who has led Tennessee to three straight trips to the Elite Eight.

Des Moines/Ames (Iowa State Cyclones, Iowa Hawkeyes): 256

Raleigh/Durham (Duke Blue Devils, UNC Tar Heels, NC State Wolfpack): 193

Indianapolis (Butler Bulldogs, Indiana Hoosiers, Purdue Boilermakers): 190

Birmingham (Alabama Crimson Tide, UAB Blazers): 185

Omaha (Creighton Blue Jays, Nebraska Cornhuskers): 180

Kansas City (Kansas Jayhawks, Kansas State Wildcats, Missouri Tigers) 173

Wichita/Hutchinson (Wichita State Shockers): 173

Charleston/Huntington (Marshall Thundering Herd, West Virginia Mountaineers): 161

Little Rock/Pine Bluff (Arkansas Razorbacks): 157

Cincinnati (Cincinnati Bearcats, Xavier Musketeers): 154

Oklahoma City (Oklahoma Sooners, Oklahoma State Cowboys): 143

Paganin: "L'Inter pensava di tagliare fuori il Milan invece è arrivata una bella scoppola"

📅 Nov 03, 2026  |  Category: Technology  |  Read Source →

L'ex calciatore Antonio Paganin è intervenuto ai microfoni della radio di Tuttomercatoweb.com, durante Maracanà, e ha parlato dell'Inter e dell'approccio dei nerazzurri nel Derby perso contro il Milan:

"È la prima volta che ho avuto la sensazione di una squadra piatta. Nel derby non ha dato la sensazione di essere l'Inter che conosciamo. Ha fatto grandissima fatica a reagire. Forse ha dato per scontato che la gara fosse più semplice del previsto. Pensavano già di tagliarli fuori invece è arrivata una bella scoppola. Forse un po' di presunzione inconscia. Sei andato incontro a 90' incolori”.
